The *Mettasutta* ("The Benefits of Love", Iti 22; PTS It 14) is a discourse preserved in the *Ekakanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. In this teaching, the Buddha declares that "acts of merit" (*puñña*) is a synonym for everything that is blissful, desirable, pleasing, endearing, and charming [SuttaCentral]. To illustrate the power of merit, the Buddha recounts the immense cosmic and heavenly fruits he personally experienced over many eons as a result of developing a mind of loving-kindness and performing meritorious deeds [SuttaCentral].

In terms of parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral lists a full parallel in the Chinese *Ekottarikāgama* (EĀ 10.7), together with passage-level parallels in the *Puññakiriyavatthu Sutta* (Iti 60), the Chinese discourse T 765.136, and the *Aṅguttaranikāya* (AN 7.62, also titled *Mettasutta*) [SuttaCentral]. The text is also cited in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37, *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*) [SuttaCentral].
